# PCB Parts MCP Server

> MCP server for electronic component data: a searchable daily snapshot of JLCPCB's in-stock catalog (630K+ parts with stock >= 10), live stock and prices from JLCPCB, Mouser and DigiKey, EasyEDA pinouts and footprints, SamacSys KiCad files, reference board schematics, sensor lookup and PCB design rules.

- Endpoint: `https://pcbparts.dev/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, stateless)
- Auth: none
- Rate limit: 100 requests a minute per IP (an IPv6 address's /64 counts as one), with `X-RateLimit-*` headers on replies (see Rate limit)
- Health: `https://pcbparts.dev/health`
- Source: https://github.com/Averyy/pcbparts-mcp

## Setup

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add -s user --transport http pcbparts https://pcbparts.dev/mcp
```

Claude Desktop and claude.ai: Customize → Connectors → "+ Add" → "Add custom connector" with the URL above (`claude_desktop_config.json` only runs local servers). Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`); VS Code (`.vscode/mcp.json`) uses the key `"servers"` instead of `"mcpServers"`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pcbparts": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://pcbparts.dev/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Clients that only run local commands (Copilot for Xcode): `{"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://pcbparts.dev/mcp"]}`.

## Which tool

- Find parts: `jlc_search`. Confirm stock before ordering, or find parts with stock under 10: `jlc_stock_check`.
- Recorded low-stock observations for one LCSC code or a BOM's list of up to 50: `jlc_stock_history`; missing scrape records are not confirmed stockouts.
- One part's live details: `jlc_get_part(lcsc=...)`. A manufacturer part number to JLCPCB parts: `jlc_get_part(mpn=...)`.
- A BOM's parts at once (stock, price tiers, library type), up to 50 LCSC codes or MPNs per call from the daily snapshot: `jlc_get_parts`. Check live with `jlc_get_part(lcsc=...)` only when a part is missing or its stock is close to the quantity needed.
- Replacement for a part: get its LCSC code (from `jlc_get_part(mpn=...)` if needed), then `jlc_find_alternatives(lcsc=...)`.
- Mouser or DigiKey data: `mouser_get_part`, `digikey_get_part`, only when JLCPCB can't answer (the part isn't at JLCPCB, or the user asked for that distributor's stock or price); their shared daily limits often run out.
- Lifecycle status (NRND, last time buy, obsolete) of one part or a BOM of up to 50: `part_lifecycle`.
- Pins and footprint pads: `jlc_get_pinout`. KiCad files: `cse_get_kicad` (slow).
- How real boards wire an IC: `board_search(component=...)`, then `board_get(slug, focus=IC)`.
- Choosing a sensor: `sensor_recommend`. Design guidance: `get_design_rules`.

## Tools

Optional filters and identity arguments default to null unless stated otherwise. Result limits are integers clamped to each tool's range. `library_type` accepts `basic`, `preferred`, `no_fee` (basic or preferred), `extended`, `all`; ignores case and surrounding whitespace; accepts `no-fee`. `packages` and `manufacturers` accept arrays, JSON-array strings or one literal string, never comma-split (max 50 items each). A JSON-string argument (`packages`, `manufacturers`, `spec_filters`, a `lcsc` list, `measure`, `tag`) holding an unpaired surrogate escape such as `\ud800` is refused with `error: "Invalid <argument>: ..."`, which shows it escaped (`jlc_get_parts` and `part_lifecycle` make it that part's error instead).

### jlc_search

Searches the daily snapshot (stock >= 10); parts kept after they left the snapshot (see `jlc_get_part`) are never in its results or counts. Stock is as of `data_as_of`; the 1-piece price is refreshed weekly, as of `prices_as_of` (a part new since then has its first scraped price).

- Arguments: `query` (max 500 characters; plain words, e.g. "100nF 25V X7R 0402"), `subcategory_name` or `subcategory_id`, `spec_filters`, `package` or `packages` (OR, max 50), `manufacturer`, `min_stock` (default 10, clamped to at least 0), `library_type`, `prefer_no_fee` (default true: basic and preferred first), `pcba_type` ("economic" or "standard_only"), `sort_by` ("stock" by default, "price" or "spec"), `sort_spec`, `sort_order`, `limit` (default 20, clamped to 1-100), `offset` (default 0, clamped to 0-10000), `strict` (default false), `match_all_terms` (default true), `facets` (default false).
- `spec_filters`: array or JSON-array string, up to 50 of `{"name", "op", "value"}`, e.g. `[{"name": "Vgs(th)", "op": "<", "value": "2V"}]`; values accept text or numbers. Operators `=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<` (`=>` normalizes to `>=`); `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` work only on numeric specs. Several `=` filters on one spec match any of the values (OR), except `Supply Voltage` and `Vin`, where a part must cover all of them (AND). Names ignore case. Unitless values use base units (V, A, ohms, F, H, Hz, W, mm, bytes). `jlc_search_help(subcategory=...)` lists a subcategory's specs, which are numeric, and which sort.
- Battery holders: a query naming a battery, cell, coin cell or button cell holder searches all holder subcategories. Sizes AA (No. 5, 14500), AAA (No. 7, 10440), C (No. 2), D (No. 1) and coin or button cell match the part's text and show as `Battery Size` in `filters_applied.spec_filters`; two sizes mean either. Other sizes (18650) are plain search words.
- Short spec names: `Vgs(th)`, `Vds`, `Id`, `Rds(on)`, `Vr`, `If`, `Vf`, `Vceo`, `Ic`, `Vout`, `Iout`, `Quiescent Current` (`Iq`), `Supply Voltage`, `Isolation Voltage`, `Capacitance`, `Resistance`, `Inductance`, `Voltage`, `Tolerance`, `Power`, `DCR`, `Isat`, `Frequency`, `Load Capacitance`, `Junction Capacitance`, `Reverse Stand-Off Voltage (Vrwm)`, `Operating Temperature` (°C).
- Sorting by a spec: `sort_spec` (e.g. "RDS(on)@4.5V", "Dropout@500mA", "Vf@1A", "Iq", "Isat") with `sort_order` "asc" (default) or "desc". A query can supply the spec instead ("lowest Iq LDO"); `sort_order` with neither, or `sort_by="spec"` without `sort_spec`, is an error. Parts that don't list the spec come last. Rows add `sort_value` (the figure sorted on); `sort` says what was compared, and `sort.note` says when figures at different test conditions were compared as listed.
- Reply: `results`, `total` (every match before pagination), `page_info` (`limit`, `offset`, `returned`), `library_type_counts`, `no_fee_available`; part-number searches add `mpn_matches` counts. Part rows: `lcsc`, `model`, `manufacturer`, `package`, `stock`, `price`, `library_type`, `preferred`, `category`, `subcategory`, `subcategory_id`, `mounting_type`, `specs`, `data_source`; optional `description` when specs are absent, and annotations below or from reviewed evidence. `filters_applied` lists every filter that ran; `parsed` what the query text gave. `relaxed` names query words, a query-only library preference or a part type left out to get results; `relaxed.dropped_filters` lists parsed spec filters dropped when a part number was retried, so those results don't meet them. `parsed.adjusted_filters` lists specs moved or left out (including a package that fell back to its bare family); `ignored_filters` filters not applied or rarely listed. `unlisted` counts parts a range filter left out only because they list no value. `hint` on an empty reply suggests a next step. `counts_complete=false` means the counts are partial. `valid_values` lists accepted inputs on an error.
- `facets=true` adds manufacturer, package and library_type counts over the full final effective search, independent of pagination. Every active filter applies, including the facet's own field. `facets` has `scope="filtered_snapshot"`, `matched_total`, `complete`, `status` ("complete", "incomplete", "unavailable") and `elapsed_ms`. Each field has up to 15 `buckets` (`value`, `count`), sorted by count descending then value, plus `omitted_buckets` and `omitted_count`. Library values are basic/preferred/extended; no_fee means basic plus preferred, not a separate bucket. Exact counts appear only with complete status; otherwise matched_total is null and buckets are absent. Facets use a private read connection with their own about 200 ms / 2,000,000 SQLite VM step / 5,000 Python-candidate budget; exhaustion preserves the search results.
- Accepted spellings: `pcba_type` ignores case, spaces and hyphens and accepts "standard" (= standard_only) and "economic_and_standard" (= economic); `sort_order` accepts ascending/lowest and descending/highest; `sort_by` ignores case.
- LDO dropout at a load: `{"name": "Dropout", "op": "<=", "value": "0.3V@500mA"}` uses each part's listed dropout at or above that load, or scales a lower test current's figure up linearly; parts rated only below the load are left out. Rows add `dropout_at_load` saying which figure was used.
- USB-PD: controller, sink, source or trigger wording selects PD controllers over USB-C connectors. Sink/trigger and source rank listed receiver/supply controllers first, and a sink voltage ranks matching negotiated Output Voltage within the role; parts missing those attributes stay in the results unless `strict=true`. Strict sink-and-source requirements are reported as unsupported.
- When the search shortens a part number (`LM1117-3.3` searches `LM1117`), `mpn_match` on each result is `full`, `same_suffix` or `family`, in that order.
- MOSFET queries with a gate drive add `rds_on_at_drive`: the RDS(on) listed at or below that drive, or null when none is listed there. Null parts stay in the results.
- `pcba_type="standard_only"` on a part means one such part moves the whole order to Standard assembly. `no_datasheet=true` means JLCPCB lists no datasheet; `no_datasheet_note` clarifies that LCSC or the manufacturer may have one.

### jlc_stock_check

Live JLCPCB search over the whole catalog (7M+ parts). Arguments: `query` (max 500 characters), `category_name`/`category_id`, `subcategory_name`/`subcategory_id`, `package`/`packages`, `manufacturer`/`manufacturers`, `library_type`, `min_stock` (default 10, clamped to at least 0; 0 includes out-of-stock), `sort_by` ("quantity" default, "price"), `page` (default 1, clamped to at least 1), `limit` (default 20, clamped to 1-100). JLCPCB matches whole part numbers and their starts, not text inside them. One LCSC code as `query` returns that part only, with its price tiers.

Reply: `results`, `page`, `per_page`, `total`, `total_pages`, `has_more`. Results use the JLC part-row fields above with live `data_source`; a single-code lookup also includes `prices` (`qty`, `price`) where listed. `hint` appears when an LCSC code matches nothing (with the min_stock and filters applied) and when a part-number fragment matches no part number from its start but is inside in-stock ones ("2812" names WS2812B).

### jlc_stock_history

Recorded events for one `lcsc` C-code: C followed by 1-12 digits (case and surrounding spaces ignored). `lcsc` can also be a list (or JSON array string) of up to 50 codes, de-duplicated: see the list reply below. Event `type` is `change`, `new`, `gone`, `reappear` or `type_change`. `days` defaults to 180, integer 1-366, ending on the newest recorded date rather than today. At most 100 events, newest first; `more_events=true` means older events in that window were omitted.

Reply: `lcsc`, `window` (`start`, `end`, `history_start`, `history_end`, inclusive ISO dates), `events` (`date`, `type`, `stock_after`, `note`, optional `stock_before`), `more_events`, `what_is_recorded` (plain-language recording limits), `current_stock` (snapshot quantity; null with `gone_since` for a part kept after it left the snapshot, its stock unknown: under 10 or no longer listed; null if neither lists it), `current_stock_as_of` (snapshot time, possibly null). An empty history DB has null window dates. Unknown codes and parts without events return `events: []` normally. A missing/unreadable history DB returns an error.

List reply: `window`, `parts`, `what_is_recorded` (once), `current_stock_as_of`. Each part, in input order: `lcsc`, `current_stock` (and `gone_since`, as for one code), `summary` over the whole window (`events` total, `gone` count, `lowest_recorded` stock of non-gone events or null, `last_gone` date or null), the newest 10 `events` (same fields and notes as one code) and `more_events`. An invalid code is `{lcsc, error}` and the others are still answered; an empty list or more than 50 codes is an error. Counts include `gone` events on suspect scrape dates; their notes say so.

Changes are recorded only when resulting stock is <=1,000 and absolute change exceeds 10 at 0-100, 25 at 101-500 or 100 at 501-1,000. An empty history does not establish stable stock: stock above 1,000 and small changes are not tracked. New records require 0 < stock <=1,000; reappear from a listed zero and library-type changes are independent of this cap. `gone` has `stock_after: null`: it means missing from a scrape, possibly delisted, below its 10-unit floor or a scrape gap, never a confirmed zero or ongoing stockout. A scrape gap that empties whole subcategories at once is not recorded as gone: those parts keep their previous stock for up to two days (the past gap days were corrected the same way). Notes label remaining disappearances on those gap dates (2026-03-03, 03-16, 03-18, 05-15) and returns within two days as `suspect_scrape`. Other dates are not certified complete; 2026-08-07 is missing. Returns above 1,000 may be unrecorded. Past events have no before-values; `stock_before` appears only when actually recorded from the previous snapshot. Current stock is separate snapshot data, not live. No predictions or availability percentages.

### jlc_get_part

- `lcsc` (e.g. "C82899"): live details, cached up to an hour.
- `mpn` (e.g. "LM358P", max 100 characters): searches the daily snapshot (stock >= 10) and returns `{mpn, results, total}`; call `jlc_get_part(lcsc=...)` on a result for live stock and full details. It also finds other dash and space spellings, the same maker's packing codes and BOM text with notes ("TL074 OP AMP"), and never a different grade. Inexact matches add `match` (`separators`, `packing`, `alias`, `alternative`, `lcsc`, `related`) and `matched_mpn`; `related` results can be other part types. Hits add `exact` (true when the number itself matched, ignoring case; false for any `match`) and `ambiguous` (true when more than one part matches: pick by `manufacturer` and `package`).
- Parts that left the snapshot: a part that drops out of the daily snapshot (a scrape no longer lists it: its stock fell under 10, or JLCPCB stopped listing it) is kept, with what the snapshot had for it, until a scrape lists it again. Kept parts answer an `mpn` when no in-stock part matches; when the in-stock matches are only full-text ones (`related`, or an `alternative` that full text found for a BOM line's other number) while a kept part matches the number; or when a kept part has the number itself (ignoring case) and the only in-stock parts are another maker's, spelled with other separators (`separators`: Molex's 2081001 gone, TE's 208100-1 in stock). In those last two cases the kept parts come first and the in-stock ones after them, which the `note` describes; the maker's own other spelling, or a `packing` match, still answers alone. They are matched by the same rules except full-text matches, most `last_stock` first, each with `stock: null` (unknown: under 10 or no longer listed, not a confirmed stockout), `gone: true`, `gone_since` (UTC date of the first scrape it was missing from), `last_stock` (its stock in the last scrape that listed it), `price` and `prices` (the last 1-piece price the snapshot had for it, which is refreshed weekly), `data_source.observed_at: null` (what was kept predates `gone_since`), no `specs` or `pcba_type`; the reply adds `hint` and `next_call` (`jlc_stock_check` with `min_stock: 0`, not executed) to check live stock. When parts in stock match the number, the reply lists only those, plus `gone_matches` (how many kept parts also match).

Provide `lcsc` or `mpn`; a nonempty `lcsc` wins when both are supplied.

Snapshot part rows carry `data_source` (`kind`, `provider`, `observed_at`, null for parts that left the snapshot, plus `specs_provider` "LCSC" when LCSC supplied the specs); live lookup observations keep their time through caching. MPN hits include `data_as_of` (stock), `prices_as_of` (the weekly 1-piece `price`) and `price_tiers_as_of`; each result adds `prices`, the quantity tiers from the daily scrape, exactly as in `jlc_get_parts` rows. Misses (no in-stock or kept match) identify snapshot scope, `availability: unknown_outside_snapshot`, and an optional unexecuted live-check `next_call`.

Reply fields: `prices` (quantity tiers), `datasheet_pdf` (a stable link to the PDF), `datasheet` (LCSC's viewer page, null when none), `maker_datasheet` (the manufacturer's link, where listed), `datasheet_note`, `specs`, `specs_note` (what the listing leaves out for the part type), `spec_evidence` (where reviewed: manufacturer values, conditions, document, printed page, source URL, review date), `spec_discrepancies` (known catalog/document conflicts; catalog specs and numeric filtering/sorting are preserved), `pcba_type`, `lcsc_url`, `min_order`, `reel_qty`, `has_easyeda_footprint` (null = unknown, false = none), `easyeda_symbol_uuid`, `easyeda_footprint_uuid`. No lifecycle status: use `part_lifecycle`.

Savings use a rounded legacy $3 Economic loading-fee estimate, labelled with `is_estimate` and `assembly_service_assumption`; confirm current quotes. Standard service differs.

### jlc_get_parts

Up to 50 parts per call from the daily snapshot (stock >= 10), for BOM refreshes and checking many parts at once. Database only: no JLCPCB, LCSC or EasyEDA request, and the whole list is one tool call against the rate limit (the requests a client sends for one call; see Rate limit). Stock is as of `data_as_of`; the 1-piece `price` is refreshed weekly, as of `prices_as_of`; `prices` lists the quantity tiers from the daily scrape, as of `price_tiers_as_of`. For one part's live stock and prices, datasheet and footprint status, use `jlc_get_part(lcsc=...)`. No specs, datasheet links, EasyEDA status or lifecycle (`jlc_get_part`, `part_lifecycle`).

- Arguments: `parts` (required): up to 50, as a list or a JSON array string (one plain string is one part; never comma-split). Each is an LCSC code string ("C7950": C and 1-12 digits; case and surrounding spaces ignored), an MPN string ("LM358P", max 100 characters), or an object `{"mpn", "manufacturer"}` (max 100 characters each; `"lcsc"` also accepted, and wins over `mpn` when both are given, so an `mpn` or `manufacturer` beside a valid `lcsc` is never checked or used; an `lcsc` that isn't an LCSC code, such as a BOM's "N/A", is set aside when `mpn` is given). The maker narrows an MPN's matches, compared loosely ("Microchip Tech" matches "Microchip Technology", "ST Microelectronics" STMicroelectronics but not JLCPCB's "ST(Semtech)"), at every match step: Comchip's own 1N4007-G answers `{"mpn": "1N4007G", "manufacturer": "Comchip"}` though other makers list 1N4007G exactly. A part number shaped like an LCSC code (2SC1815's "C1815") needs `{"mpn": "C1815"}` when that code is a listed part; a plain code string that neither the snapshot nor the kept parts list is also looked up as a part number (2SC945's "C945"), and its row is then an MPN row with a `note` saying so. Repeated inputs are answered again, in place. Any item type is accepted (a wrong one is that row's `error`).
- Reply: `data_as_of`, `prices_as_of`, `price_tiers_as_of` (when the tiers in `prices` were scraped; null when the server has none loaded), `total` (rows), `counts` (`found`: in the snapshot; `gone`: answered from parts kept after they left it; `not_found`; `error`; they add up to `total`), `results` (one row per input, in input order) and, when any row is gone or `not_found`, one `hint` (what a gone row is; the snapshot lists in-stock parts only; `jlc_get_part(lcsc=...)` looks a code up live, `jlc_stock_check(query=...)` finds low or zero stock; part numbers match only as themselves, never by text, and `jlc_search` finds values such as 10k). `input` is each part as given; a string over 100 characters is cut to its first 100 and "...", and anything else whose JSON is over 200 characters becomes the first 100 characters of that JSON and "...".
- LCSC code row: `input` (exactly as given), `lcsc`, `model`, `manufacturer`, `package`, `stock`, `price` (1 piece, weekly), `prices` (quantity tiers in `jlc_get_part`'s shape, `[{"qty": "1+", "price"}, {"qty": "1000+", "price"}, ...]`, from the daily scrape; trailing tiers that only repeat the price before them are left out; just `[{"qty": "1+", "price": price}]` when `price_tiers_as_of` is null or the part had no tiers in that scrape; absent when the part has no price), `library_type`, `preferred`, `pcba_type` (where known), `category`, `subcategory`, `description` (the catalog's text, possibly empty), and `no_datasheet: true` when JLCPCB lists no datasheet. Gone (left the snapshot, kept until a scrape lists it again, as in `jlc_get_part(mpn=...)`): the same fields with `stock: null` (unknown), `price`/`prices` from the last scrape that listed it, no `pcba_type` or `no_datasheet`, plus `gone: true`, `gone_since` and `last_stock`; its `price`/`prices` are the last 1-piece price the snapshot had for it (refreshed weekly). Neither: `{input, lcsc, not_found: true}`.
- MPN row, matched as `jlc_get_part(mpn=...)` matches but never by full text (no `related` results, nor `alternative` ones full text found): a number only text mentions, or a value such as "10k", is `not_found` (search values with `jlc_search`). `input`, `mpn` (trimmed), `total` (every match for the maker given), `exact`, `ambiguous`, `results` (the first 10 by stock, each with `lcsc`, `model`, `manufacturer`, `package`, `stock`, `price`, `prices`, `library_type`, `preferred` and, for a gone part, `gone`, `gone_since` and `last_stock`: the part's description and category are in its LCSC code's row), plus `match`, `matched_mpn` and `note` for inexact matches, as in `jlc_get_part`. With no match in stock for the maker given, its gone matches are the `results` (gone rows; the row counts as `gone`, and adds `other_manufacturers` when other makers' parts are in stock); when a gone part has the number itself and the only ones in stock are another maker's spelled with other separators, the gone parts come first and those after them, with a `note`, as in `jlc_get_part`; with matches in stock, `gone_matches` counts the gone ones. No match: `{input, mpn, total: 0, results: [], not_found: true}`, plus `other_manufacturers` (up to 10 names) when the number is listed in stock only under other makers.
- A row with `error` is an unusable input (a BOM placeholder such as DNP, an empty string, a wrong type, an invalid `lcsc` with no `mpn`, over 100 characters, control characters such as a NUL, tab or line break, an unpaired surrogate escape such as `\ud800` in a JSON array string, which `input` echoes as that escape; with a valid `lcsc` only the code counts), or `"Database not available"` when the database failed on that number alone (a plain code string's lookup as a part number included); the other rows are still answered. Call errors: an empty list, more than 50 parts, an invalid JSON array, the database unavailable.

### jlc_get_pinout

`lcsc` or `uuid` (EasyEDA symbol; a nonempty `lcsc` wins), `footprint` (default false; needs `lcsc`). Reply: `lcsc`, `model`, `manufacturer`, `package` (these four may be null with UUID-only lookup), `pin_count`, `pins`, `easyeda_symbol_uuid`. Pin numbers and names exactly as the EasyEDA symbol has them; numbers match the EasyEDA footprint's pads. `electrical` appears only where the symbol sets it. `unverified` (the string "Symbol not verified by LCSC") is present when LCSC hasn't verified the symbol. `note`: the pins are named only by number, or a diode/LED-type part whose numbering varies between sources (connect it by pin name). `footprint=true` adds `footprint` with name, `source_link`, `pad_count`, `numbered_pads`, `pitch`, `pad_sizes` and `pads` (number, x, y in mm from the origin with y down, shape, size, layer, hole, slot_length); if the footprint can't be fetched, the pins still come back with `footprint_error`.

Empty `jlc_search` responses can include `why_empty`: tested library/package/stock changes, retained constraints, counts with exact/at_least relation, executable next calls where representable, and `diagnostics_complete`, plus `status` when the checks didn't finish: "budget_exhausted_or_busy" (out of time or the snapshot was busy) or "diagnostic_failed". Only the stock>=10 snapshot is checked. Diagnostics are bounded to three queries/200 ms; incomplete work is explicit and original results remain empty. Negative Vout preserves polarity; impedance@frequency compares that frequency; part-number exclusions are reported as unsupported.

### jlc_find_alternatives

`lcsc` (required LCSC code), `library_type`, `same_package` (default false), `has_easyeda_footprint` (true/false filter, default null: no filter), `min_stock` (default 10, clamped to at least 0), `limit` (per list, default 10, clamped to 1-50), `board_quantity` and `placements_per_board` (default 1, each a positive integer up to 1,000,000, for `comparison.savings`), `land_compatible` (default false).

- `summary.found` counts `alternatives`: parts whose primary value and required specs match (connector series and contacts, transistor polarity, regulator output and listed input range) and whose readable ratings are the same or better. Ranked basic/preferred first.
- Ratings that are missing or unreadable don't disqualify a part: they're listed in `specs_unparseable`. `unchecked_requirements` lists what wasn't checked; pinout and external circuit always need checking. A regulator's single input rating checks only the maximum.
- `unverified_alternatives` miss a required match or lack comparable rating conditions: compare by hand. Inductor Isat needs comparable inductance-drop criteria and rating bases; thermal current needs matching thermal conditions and bases; DCR needs comparable published bases. Multi-diode current comparisons need loading/thermal evidence. These candidates do not drive the recommended savings comparison.
- `has_easyeda_footprint` checks at most `min(2 * limit, 15)` candidates after library/package eligibility; unknown availability is excluded for both true and false. Extended fallback examples use only the remaining check budget when no verified no-fee result was found. `summary.footprint_filter` reports either cap and lookup failures.
- `summary.stages`: `retrieval` counts per source (`retrieved`, `limit`, `hit_limit`, `error`: null or "retrieval_failed"; database also `scanned`, `scan_limit`, `scan_hit_limit`); `primary` and `specs` counts (`passed`, `failed`, `unknown`); `eligibility.library/package` passed/failed; `footprints` checked/compatible/incompatible/unknown, `not_checked_cap`, `eligible_checked`, `fallback_checked`; `output` per-list truncation counts and `limit_per_list`. Retrieval counts precede deduplication and source-specific filtering; subsequent stages describe the merged candidates. Unknown spec counts include unreadable ratings and do not change verified/manual classification. Bounds reached do not prove more matches exist; retrieval errors remain visible alongside any usable results.
- `land_compatible=true` (for a board whose copper is already made) compares the top 30 candidates' EasyEDA footprint pads with the original's and adds `land` to each: `fits` (same pad count and pad kinds, every pad centre within 0.15 mm), `turn` (0/90/180/270 degrees counter-clockwise, top view, the candidate's footprint is turned to line up; non-zero changes the pick-and-place rotation), `max_offset_mm`, and `renumbered` (original pad number -> the candidate's pad number in the same place, only where they differ; each footprint author's numbering, so a renumbered pad 1 needs both datasheets checked). Order: fits as drawn with the same numbers, then only other pads renumbered, then fits only turned, then pad 1 elsewhere, then not compared, then no fit; the usual ranking within each. `land: null` means not compared (no known footprint, or the fetch was skipped); `summary.stages.land` counts `checked`, `fits`, `fits_turned`, `pin1_moved`, `no_fit`, `unknown` (with `unknown_reasons`), `fetched`, `not_checked_cap`, and `original` when the original's footprint isn't known. Pin functions aren't compared. `summary.land_note` explains the fields. Footprints are fetched once and stored, so a repeat check takes no extra time.
- Connector alternatives list `land pattern and pin 1 position` in `unchecked_requirements`, and without `land_compatible` the reply's `summary.land_note` says makers' footprints for one series differ.
- Part types without rules return `similar_parts`. RF parts are ordered by `frequency_coverage` of the original's range. Modules and others list the same package and part family first, marked `likely_drop_in` (pinout unchecked).
- Lifecycle (NRND) isn't checked.
- Reply: `original`, `search_criteria`, `summary`; part types with rules add `alternatives`, `unverified_alternatives`, `comparison` (`original`, `recommended`, `savings`) and `confidence` (`level` high/medium/low, `reason`, `unchecked_requirements`); others add `similar_parts` and `manual_comparison`. Rows add `score`, `score_breakdown`, `specs_verified`, `specs_unparseable`, `unchecked_requirements`, and where they apply `verification_status`, `unverified_requirements`, `moq_warning`, `package_warning`.
- `comparison.savings`: `unit_price_diff` remains the qty-1 price difference. `original_unit_price_at_quantity`, `replacement_unit_price_at_quantity` and `unit_price_diff_at_quantity` give the prices and difference used in `order_total = assembly_fee + unit_price_diff_at_quantity * component_quantity`, where `component_quantity = board_quantity * placements_per_board`. `price_basis` is `"price breaks at component_quantity"` when both parts have tiers and that quantity reaches a break above the first for either part: each part then uses its largest break starting at or below that quantity, except that a part below its own second break uses its qty-1 `price` (the snapshot's first break is the daily scrape's, `price` the weekly or a live one). The original's tiers are live; the replacement's are from the daily snapshot, dated by `savings.price_tiers_as_of`. Otherwise (either part lacks tiers, or neither reaches its second break, as at the default quantity 1) both use their qty-1 `price`, `price_basis` is `"qty 1"` and `price_tiers_as_of` is null, so `order_total` is `assembly_fee + unit_price_diff * component_quantity`. Part `price` fields and ranking still use qty 1. `order_total` is null when a needed price is unknown; assembly fees remain a rounded legacy $3 Economic estimate, not an order quote.

### jlc_search_help

No arguments: all categories. `category` (name string or integer ID): its subcategories. `subcategory` (name string or integer ID, takes precedence over category): its filterable specs with type and example values, marked `sort_spec` where sortable.

Replies: no arguments `{categories: [{id, name, count, subcategory_count}]}`; category `{category_id, category_name, subcategories: [{id, name, count}]}`; subcategory `{subcategory_id, subcategory_name, category_name, sample_size, attributes}`, each attribute `{name, alias, type, count, example_values, values, min, max, total_unique, sort_spec}` where present. Attributes are sampled from up to 1,000 parts of the subcategory; `values` holds at most 50, and `total_unique` appears when there are more. An unknown category returns `error` and `hint`.

### mouser_get_part

`part_number` (required, max 500 characters total): a Mouser PN or MPN (3-40 characters each), or up to 10 joined by "|" ("595-LM358P|NE555P"), one request per call, or two when a broad number fills the reply: Mouser returns at most 50 results per request, so the numbers a broad one crowded out (without their own part in the reply) are asked once more without it, within the shared limits; one still left out is listed in `not_found` for that reply only and isn't kept. A number that can't be a Mouser part number isn't sent and costs no request: it's in `not_found`, and `not_sent` gives its reason (see "Numbers not sent" below). Matching is loose: use full part numbers when batching and match results to the numbers asked by `requested` and `matched_by` (below). Check `manufacturer`: a number can match another maker's part. JST's `(LF)` and `(SN)` endings may be given or left off, as in `digikey_get_part`; other bracketed endings (`(UMW)`, Hirose `(50)`) must match. `lifecycle` is Mouser's status where it gives one (Not Recommended for New Designs, End of Life, Obsolete, Discontinued), else null; `lifecycle_status` is `active`, `nrnd`, `last_time_buy`, `obsolete` or `unknown` (null counts as `active`, Discontinued as `unknown`). For lifecycle checks use `part_lifecycle`.

Each part number's answer is kept 3 days (not found: 1 day; nothing for a number a 50-result reply may have crowded out) and shared by every caller: a batch sends only the numbers not kept yet, and nothing when all are kept. Kept answers don't count against the daily limit.

Reply: `{results, total, observed_at}`, optional `not_found` listing unmatched inputs (and those not sent) and `not_sent` (`{number: reason}`). When a shared limit holds back the numbers not kept yet while others were kept, the reply has the kept ones' results plus `not_checked` (the numbers not looked up) and `retry_after` (seconds), and no `error`; with none kept, it's the limit error. `lookup_failed` lists numbers Mouser returned an error for (each is asked alone once when Mouser rejects a batch, so the others still answer). Results are grouped by the numbers asked, in order. `observed_at` (UTC, ISO 8601) is when Mouser gave the oldest answer used. Each result: `source`, `part_number`, `mfr_part_number`, `manufacturer`, `description`, `category`, `stock`, `price`, `price_breaks` (`qty`, `price`, `currency`), `datasheet_url`, `product_url`, `rohs`, `lifecycle`, `lifecycle_status`, `parameters`, `min_qty`, `currency`, `unit_weight_g`, `requested`, `matched_by`.

`requested` is the number asked (as given, trimmed) that the result answers, or null when a result can't be put down to one of the numbers given: in a batch, two of them could have found it; or it matches none of them (Mouser can return such parts for a batch, or for a request shared with other callers' numbers). When two numbers given are each the part itself (`595-LM358P|LM358P`), it answers the first. `matched_by` is how it matches that number (null when `requested` is), the first of these that applies: `exact` (its MPN is the number, ignoring case), `separators` (also ignoring `-`, space, `_` and `/`), `packing` (a JST part's MPN once its `(LF)`/`(SN)` endings are set aside), `mouser_pn` (the number is its Mouser PN, compared as for `separators`): these four are the part asked for. `prefix` (its MPN or Mouser PN starts with the number, ignoring case and punctuation: Mouser's loose match, so a longer and maybe different part number, such as LM358PE4 for LM358P) and `other` (Mouser returned it for the number by a rule of its own, as it can for a lone number) need checking. `exact` and `separators` mean what they do in `jlc_get_part`'s `match`; `packing` here is only JST's `(LF)`/`(SN)` endings (`jlc_get_part`'s `packing` also covers tape, reel and lead-free suffixes).

### digikey_get_part

`product_number` (required, max 500 characters): one DigiKey PN or full MPN per call (one keyword search per lookup; a partial number can find nothing and still uses a request; a miss includes a `hint` suggesting a DigiKey PN unless the input already ends in `-ND`). A number that can't be a DigiKey part number isn't sent: its miss adds `not_sent` (the reason, see "Numbers not sent") and a `hint` saying why. JST's `(LF)` and `(SN)` endings may be given or left off; `mfr_part_number` is DigiKey's spelling (`matched_by` is then `packing`). `part_number`, `price`, `price_breaks` and `min_qty` are one packaging's (the PN given, else the smallest order); `packaging` names it and `other_packaging` lists the rest. `lifecycle` is DigiKey's product status; `lifecycle_status` is `active` (Active), `nrnd` (Not For New Designs), `last_time_buy` (Last Time Buy, or an end-of-life part still marked Active), `obsolete` or `unknown` (Discontinued at Digi-Key and anything else). Each number's answer is kept 3 days (not found: 1 day; case is ignored) and shared by every caller. For lifecycle checks use `part_lifecycle`.

Reply: `{results, total, observed_at}` (`observed_at`: when DigiKey answered, UTC ISO 8601). A number several makers use returns each maker's listing, most stock first. Each result has the shared Mouser fields above except `unit_weight_g`; its `price_breaks` contain only `qty` and `price`, using the result's `currency`. Optional `packaging`, `other_packaging` (`part_number`, `packaging`, `min_qty`, `price`), `reel_fee`/`marketplace` on the result or other packaging, and `last_buy_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, DigiKey's last order date) where DigiKey gives one. Every result has `requested` (the number asked, trimmed) and `matched_by` as in `mouser_get_part`, with `digikey_pn` (the number is the result's `part_number`, DigiKey's PN for the packaging described) in place of `mouser_pn`; `other` is a listing DigiKey gave as an exact match whose MPN and PN both differ from the number. A miss is `{error: "Part not found: ...", hint}`, plus `not_sent` for a number not sent.

### part_lifecycle

Lifecycle status for up to 50 parts per call, from Mouser and DigiKey. Readings are kept 90 days (a week when the distributor states no usable status, 30 days when it doesn't list the number) and shared by every caller; every `mouser_get_part` and `digikey_get_part` answer adds to them. A part with no reading kept is looked up on Mouser (up to 10 numbers per request; Mouser's 3-day answers count), then on DigiKey (one request each) only if Mouser doesn't list it for the maker given or Mouser's daily limit is spent (a part Mouser lists, even with a status it can't name, isn't sent to DigiKey). A Mouser per-minute limit leaves the part `unknown` with `retry_after`, and a failed Mouser lookup leaves it `unknown` with `lookup_failed`; DigiKey isn't asked then. Nothing is sent for a number neither distributor can list: such parts are `unknown` with `not_sent`. Its answers are kept like `mouser_get_part`'s and `digikey_get_part`'s. No cap on lookups per call besides the shared daily and per-minute limits.

- Arguments: `parts` (required): up to 50, as a list or a JSON array string (one plain string is one part; never comma-split). Each is an MPN string ("LM358P", max 100 characters), an LCSC code string ("C7950", resolved to its MPN and maker from the catalog snapshot: in-stock parts, and parts that have left it since 2026-11-12), or an object `{"mpn", "manufacturer"}` (max 100 characters each; `"lcsc"` also accepted, and supplies the MPN or maker that isn't given or can't be used: an MPN no distributor can list (a reason in "Numbers not sent" below: a value such as 10k, an LCSC code, a placeholder such as N/A, not 3-40 characters, not ASCII), containing "|", over 100 characters or with control characters, or a maker over 100 characters or with control characters; a usable MPN given wins over the catalog's; one that isn't an LCSC code, such as a BOM's "N/A", is set aside when `mpn` is given). Any item type is accepted (a wrong one is that row's `error`). The maker picks among parts several makers number the same; maker names are compared loosely ("Microchip Tech" matches "Microchip Technology"). MPNs are compared ignoring case and `-`, space, `_` and `/`, and for JST parts their `(LF)`/`(SN)` endings; a distributor's "not listed" holds only for the spelling asked (ignoring case), so "LM358P" is still looked up after "LM358-P" wasn't found.
- Reply: `{results, total, status_counts}`, plus `retry_after` (the smallest of the results') when any part waited on a limit. `results` has one entry per input, in input order: `input` (as given; a string over 100 characters is cut to its first 100 and "...", anything else whose JSON is over 200 characters becomes the first 100 characters of that JSON and "..."), `lcsc` (for LCSC inputs), `mpn` (the MPN looked up), `status`, and for a reading `manufacturer`, `raw` (the distributor's wording), `source` (`mouser` or `digikey`), `observed_at` (UTC, ISO 8601, when the distributor said it) and `last_buy_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, DigiKey's) where given. `status_counts` counts each status over all results.
- `status`: `active`, `nrnd` (not recommended for new designs), `last_time_buy`, `obsolete` or `unknown`. Mouser leaves the status blank for normal active parts: a part it lists without one is `active` with `raw` "not stated by Mouser" (DigiKey isn't asked then). Mouser: Not Recommended for New Designs = `nrnd`, End of Life = `last_time_buy`, Obsolete = `obsolete`, New Product/New at Mouser = `active`, Discontinued = `unknown`. DigiKey: as in `digikey_get_part`. With readings from both, a stated status wins over Mouser's blank, then the newest.
- `unknown` results say why: `not_found: true` with `observed_at` (neither distributor lists the number), `retry_after` (seconds until a limit lets it be looked up: Mouser's per-minute limit, or the daily ones; not an error), `lookup_failed: true` (the Mouser lookup failed, or DigiKey's when it was asked, or Mouser's 50-result cap left the number out of its reply), `not_sent` (no request went out: a reason from "Numbers not sent" below), `error` (an unusable input: a BOM placeholder such as DNP, which also has `not_sent: "placeholder"`, an MPN containing "|", an LCSC code not in the catalog snapshot with a `hint`, a wrong type or length, control characters such as a NUL, tab or line break, an unpaired surrogate escape such as `\ud800` in a JSON array string, which `input` echoes as that escape), or `makers`. `makers` lists each maker's reading (`manufacturer`, `status`, `raw`, `source`, `observed_at`, `last_buy_date` where given) when several makers list the number and none was given (`status` is then their common status, else `unknown`), or when a maker was given but only other makers list the number (`manufacturer` is then the maker given).
- Call errors: no Mouser or DigiKey credentials on the server, an empty list, more than 50 parts, an invalid JSON array.

#### Numbers not sent

`mouser_get_part`, `digikey_get_part` and `part_lifecycle` send no request (and spend none of the shared limits) for a number no distributor can list; `not_sent` names the reason: `value` (a component value rather than a part number, alone or with a package, tolerance or rating such as "100nF 50V 0603": a number with a unit, SI-prefixed or not, such as "4.7uF", "3.3mA", "16Ω" or "1.5A", or a resistor code with its multiplier as the decimal point or after a decimal number, such as "4k7", "1R5" or "15.8k", with at most 3 significant digits; or a bare code, a whole number and a multiplier letter, such as "10k", "100R" or "2200R", with at most 2, zeros before and after left out; anything else is sent as a part number, such as Hammond's "1590A", "1590K", "193M" or "158M", "100V", or "158k"; use `jlc_search` to find parts by value), `lcsc_code` (an LCSC code such as C7950: give the MPN, or pass the code to `part_lifecycle` as a plain string), `placeholder` (DNP, N/A, TBD and the like), `length` (not 3-40 characters; `mouser_get_part` keeps its error for those), `not_ascii` (characters part numbers don't use). Real part numbers such as 1N4148, LM358 or 0805B103K500NT are always sent.

### cse_search, cse_get_kicad

SamacSys ComponentSearchEngine; slow: a search takes about 15 s, longer when busy; answers are cached. No overall tool deadline. Search HTTP requests use `CSE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` (default 45 s per request phase); a non-Success API status is retried once after 3 s. Model downloads use a fixed 30 s timeout per request phase.

- `cse_search`: required `query` (max 500 characters), `limit` (default 5, clamped to 1-10); no credentials needed. Reply: `{results, total}`. Each result: `source`, `mfr_part_number`, `manufacturer`, `description`, `datasheet_url`, `has_model` (generic ECAD availability), `has_3d`, `model_quality`, `cse_part_id`, `pin_count`, `image_url`. Individual KiCad/Eagle/Altium formats are not confirmed.
- `cse_get_kicad`: `query` (string, max 500 characters) or `part_id` (integer), both default null; at least one needed, a nonzero `part_id` wins. Query selection takes the first search result with `has_model` and `cse_part_id`, with no separate best-match scoring. Requires `CSEARCH_USER` and `CSEARCH_PASS`. Reply: `part_id`, search metadata fields above when resolved by query, `kicad_symbol` (`.kicad_sym` text), `kicad_footprint` (`.kicad_mod` text); either file may be null. Archives over 50 MiB are rejected; files over 10 MiB are skipped.

### board_search, board_get

`board_search`: `component` (IC name, max 200 characters; adds a cross-board `consensus` when 2+ boards match), `query` (max 500 characters; function, e.g. "motor driver"), `tag` (one string, list or JSON-array string, AND semantics; ignores case/surrounding whitespace, `usb-c` aliases `usb`; lists discard nonstrings/items over 200 characters after normalization, then keep at most 10), `org` (max 200 characters), `layers`, `limit` (default 10, clamped to 1-50). Unknown tags return `valid_values`. Consensus `pct` divides by `consensus.board_count`.

Search reply: `{total, results}`; each result has `slug`, `name`, `org`, `org_display`, `source`, `source_url`, `format`, `description`, `key_coverage`, `tags`, `key_ics`, `layers`, `width_mm`, `height_mm`, `component_count`, `ic_count`, plus `matched_by` when a filter explains the match. Tag-only browsing of one tag may add `tag_consensus`; empty results may add `hint`. A `query` with no searchable words (only stop words such as board, design and pcb, or single characters; quotes and OR are not operators) browses the catalog, keeping the other filters, and the reply's `note` says so.

`board_get`: required `slug` (1-200 characters), `focus` (max 200 characters; IC name, ref like "J1", or value words like "USB-C": returns that part's pin-by-pin neighborhood), `include_bom` (default false; adds plain passives), `include_nets` (default false; full netlist, can be 100 KB+).

Detail reply: board identity/metadata fields above (without `matched_by`), plus `min_trace`, `min_clearance`, `min_drill`, `min_via`, `net_count`. Without focus: `components`, `neighborhoods` summaries, `passives_omitted` when any plain passives were hidden. Components carry `ref`, `value`, `footprint` and available descriptions/ratings/annotations, plus the design files' `mpn`, `manufacturer`, `lcsc`, `mouser`, `digikey` where listed. With focus: `focus` (`ref`, `value`, `pins`), `focus_match_type` (ref/exact/partial), optional `consensus` and `focus_alternatives`. `power_pins` and `pin_nets` appear on focus only when present; `pins_in_nets` counts the named pins in nets; `pin_count` and `nc_pins` appear where source pin information exists (`{}` means all connected). A focus miss adds `focus_error`, `available_ics` and, when present, `available_refs`. `include_nets=true` adds `nets`, `positions`, `copper_pours`. Unknown slug errors may add `did_you_mean`.

### sensor_recommend

`query` (max 500 characters), `measure` (one string, list or JSON-array string of up to 20), `type`, `protocol`, `platform` ("arduino", "esphome", "micropython", "circuitpython", "tasmota", "zephyr", "raspberry_pi"), `limit` (default 15, clamped to 1-100). Unknown measure, protocol and platform values return `valid_values`; an unknown type returns no matches. Ordering: exact normalized query-ID/alias matches first, then `platform_count` descending, then name ascending. Not for buying: use `jlc_search`.

Measures in a list all must match. `imu` expands to acceleration/gyroscope/magnetic_field with OR for a scalar or singleton list; in a multi-item list all expanded measures are required. Measure aliases include heart rate/blood oxygen→biometric, barometric→pressure, lux→light, dust→particulate and compass→magnetic_field. Protocols: i2c/i3c/spi/uart/analog/pwm/gpio/one_wire/rs485/rs232/can/i2s/usb/ble/hdq/ssi (accepted values come from the catalog; an unknown one returns `valid_values`); `gpio` includes gpio/analog/pwm/one_wire, `digital` includes gpio/pwm/one_wire, `1-wire`/`one-wire` alias one_wire. Measure/protocol/platform/type filters ignore case and surrounding whitespace.

Reply: `{total, results}`, plus `note` when `query` has no searchable words (stop words, single letters, symbols), which leaves only the filters; each result has `id`, `name`, `manufacturer`, `type`, `voltage`, `datasheet_url`, `platform_count`, `description`, `source_tier`, `measures`, `protocols`, `platforms`, `urls`, plus optional evidence fields below.

`voltage` is the supply in volts, "min-max" or a single value. Parts sold in separate supply versions or with separate supply modes list each, e.g. "3.0-3.6 or 4.5-5.5" (pick the version you order); a record covering several chips gives the range all of them support. Null when the part has no supply of its own (passive elements, probes, heated gas cells) or no maker source states one. A `capability_note` covers other rails (LED, VDDIO, mains) and a narrower supply that full specifications need (DS1821: accuracy and 1-Wire timing at 3.6-5.5V).

Sensor capability notes: calculated CO2 (CCS811, ENS160, ENS161, SGP30, iAQ-Core, APC1, SM300D2) is under `eco2`, not `co2`; BME680 and BME688 note that Bosch's BSEC library calculates IAQ and CO2 equivalent on the host. `capability_note` says what such a part really outputs. CCS811, ENS160 and SGP30 also have `compensation_inputs` and operating/stress `voltage_evidence`; compensation inputs are not selectable direct measurements. For ENS160, ENS161 and the ENS16x library the listed voltage is VDD (1.71-1.98V); VDDIO is separate (1.71-3.6V). Descriptions prefer device/integration sources over breakout marketing.

### get_design_rules

`topic` (default `""`; non-index topics truncated to 500 characters): empty or index (`INDEX.md`) returns `INDEX.md`, which lists every file. Exact normalized keys (`power/ldo`), aliases (`type-c`, `lipo`, `ws2812`, `debounce`, `nordic`, `fiducial`) and token-boundary category/filename matching select files; MCU family prefixes such as `stm32g0` also match. Otherwise a scored text fallback selects the files discussing the topic most.

Reply: `{content, matched_files, topic}`, with `note` on text-fallback matches. Up to three matching files return full content; more than three return a key list asking for a narrower topic. No matches returns the index with an explanation and empty `matched_files`.

## How jlc_search reads a query

- Units: `u`/`µ`/`μ` mean micro, `4u7` is 4.7uF (4.7uH for inductors), `6V3` is 6.3V. `10M`/`10Meg` are megaohms, `10m` milliohms. A value has at most 4 significant digits before a unit letter (`1000R`, `4R75`); a longer run such as `9774025151R` is searched as a part number. A part number, including one that starts with 7+ digits (`61300211121`, `10118194-0001LF`), is searched on its own; other words in the query are listed in `parsed.detected.not_searched` (`strict=true` keeps them). Package `1005` is `0402`.
- A value goes to the spec the part type lists: `5V relay` is the coil voltage, `3.3V LDO` the output, `12V buck` an output range covering 12V, `3.3V level shifter` a supply range covering it, `24V input 3.3V output` both sides of a regulator. A current under 1mA in an LDO/DC-DC query is the quiescent current. A resistance with an ohm unit on MOSFETs, load switches or inductors is a maximum RDS(on) or DCR. If the part type doesn't list the spec, the value is left out and `parsed.adjusted_filters` says so.
- In a MOSFET query, a voltage next to `logic level`, `GPIO` or `MCU` (up to 5V) or `gate`/`Vgs` (up to 20V) is the gate drive; parts with RDS(on) listed at or below it rank first.
- Comparisons in the text keep their operator: `Iq < 10uA`, `Vf < 0.3V`. A sign before a bare value applies to the main rating (`10uF capacitor < 25V`).
- Ranges (supply/output voltage, operating temperature): `=` matches a range that includes the value, `>=` one that reaches it, `<=` one that goes down to it. `-40°C` in a query means rated down to -40°C, `105C` up to 105°C.
- Connectors filter on pin count and pitch where the connector type lists them (`JST PH 2 pin`); `qwiic`/`STEMMA QT` mean 4-pin 1.0mm JST SH, `Grove` 4-pin 2.0mm. A query searches one pitch: a second mm length is left out (`parsed.detected.not_searched`) unless named. Headers take named lengths: `insulation height 5mm` (also body/plastic height), `mating pin length`, `tail length`, with `at least`, `under`, `>` etc.; `Insulation Height`, `Length of Mating Pin` and `Length of End Connection Pin` are numeric, so `spec_filters` can use `>`, `<` and ranges on them.
- Packages include their other spellings: `SOT-23` includes `SOT-23-3`, `0603` includes `1608`, a bare `QFN-32` matches VQFN/WQFN/UQFN of any body. `QFN-24-EP(4x4)` keeps the body and exposed pad; if no catalog package has that body, the bare family is matched and `parsed.adjusted_filters` says so (`strict=true` doesn't fall back).
- `basic`, `preferred` and `no fee` in the query set the library filter; `cheapest` sorts by price; `lowest Iq`, `highest Isat`, `most flash` sort by that spec. Arguments win over query words; `library_type="all"` overrides a library word.
- Query words that match nothing together with the rest are left out and named in `relaxed`. With `subcategory_name` or `spec_filters` given, they aren't left out: the reply is empty and `hint` names them. `strict=true` turns off every relaxation and returns an error for unsupported constraints.
- Spec figures are JLCPCB's listings; check datasheets before choosing.

## Library types

| Type | Economic loading fee | Meaning |
|------|--------------|---------|
| `basic` | none | JLCPCB's standard library |
| `preferred` | none | Recommended parts with good availability |
| `extended` | Fee per unique type; calculator uses a rounded $3 estimate | Everything else |
| `no_fee` | none | Filter for basic and preferred together |
| `all` | | No library filter |

## Rate limit

Each IPv4 address, or IPv6 /64 (all the addresses that share its first 64 bits count as one), may send 100 HTTP requests in any rolling minute. An address in the AI platforms' published outbound ranges (Anthropic's, which claude.ai and Claude connectors call from, and OpenAI's ChatGPT connectors list) may send 1,000, since many of their users share each one; it's counted by itself. Each MCP message (`initialize`, `tools/call`, ...) is one request, so a stateless client's tool call is about three. `/health` is never refused or counted; `/mcp/stats` counts like any request. A request body over 1 MB gets HTTP 413 `{error}`, whether its `Content-Length` says so or it's sent in chunks.

- Replies carry `X-RateLimit-Limit` (requests a minute for your address), `X-RateLimit-Remaining` (requests left in the current minute) and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (whole seconds until your oldest counted request leaves the minute, so one more is allowed; 0 when none are counted); `/health` replies too, without counting. Not on the few errors sent before the limit is checked (413 for a declared `Content-Length` over 1 MB, 421/403 for an unknown Host or Origin); a 413 for a body cut off as it arrives has them (it was counted).
- Over the limit: HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header (seconds, at least 1) and a JSON body `{error, retry_after, reason, resets_at, tell_user}`: `retry_after` is the same seconds, `resets_at` that moment in UTC (ISO 8601), `tell_user` one sentence to show the user, `reason` why:
  - `per_ip_rate_limit`: your address sent its limit in the last minute.
  - `too_many_clients`: the server is serving as many addresses as it can at once; not caused by your use.
  - `server_busy`: a database worker pool is overloaded (12 calls waiting, counting `tools/call` requests accepted whose tool hasn't started yet, or the oldest waiting 0.5 s, by default). Only new `tools/call` requests are refused for this reason; `initialize`, notifications, `tools/list` and other methods still pass this check. Live lookups waiting on upstream services don't contribute to database pressure. Wait the short computed `retry_after` (2-5 seconds); for this refusal `X-RateLimit-Remaining` is 0 and `X-RateLimit-Reset` is that retry delay. It counts against your address's allowance like an answered request, so retrying faster than `retry_after` runs into `per_ip_rate_limit`. While the server is busy, a request body that hasn't all arrived within 2 seconds gets this refusal too. `/health` and `/mcp/stats` never get it.
  - `datasheet_rate_limit`: only from `/mcp/datasheet/<lcsc>` (`jlc_get_part`'s `datasheet_pdf` link): the server signs at most 20 new datasheet links a minute for all its users; not caused by your use. Its `X-RateLimit-*` headers still describe your address. A `datasheet_pdf` link `jlc_get_part` returned in the last 25 minutes opens without signing.
- Requests refused for `per_ip_rate_limit` or `too_many_clients` aren't counted (a `server_busy` one is): wait `retry_after` seconds, then send again. For heavy use, self-host: https://github.com/Averyy/pcbparts-mcp#self-hosting

## Quotas

The Mouser and DigiKey daily limits are shared by everyone on pcbparts.dev (DigiKey's resets at 00:00 UTC), with at most 25 requests a minute for Mouser and 100 for DigiKey. Answers kept from earlier lookups (3 days per part, lifecycle 90 days) cost nothing. Batch Mouser lookups, look up one DigiKey part at a time, use `part_lifecycle` for lifecycle, and don't retry a quota error. Self-hosting with your own keys gives your own limits: https://github.com/Averyy/pcbparts-mcp#self-hosting
